role: The abstract pressure-plate base: the plate's thin bounds, its floor-support check and its power-state machine that the stone, wooden and weighted plates share.
scope_reason: In scope: stone and wooden plates are craftable and placeable, and entities stand on them (a villager on a house's table plate ran func_150062_a in golem-fight-s42, village-rain-s42 and village-siege-s42). world.conf redstone = off zeroes World's power queries (World.java:3511, 3585) but not the plate's own state machine: func_150062_a still writes the pressed metadata, notifies two cells and re-arms its tick. Only the power it emits (isProvidingWeakPower, isProvidingStrongPower) reaches nothing.

notes: The subclass records (BlockButtonStone is a button, the stone/wooden plates are anonymous subclasses inside BlockPressurePlate and BlockPressurePlateWeighted) inherit the support pop, which IS ported: blockcb.c:2268 drops a plate with no floor. Placement is exercised by the place probes (out/java/place/big2 covers all ids in its 40000-case sweep). idxaudit 2026-09-27: was switched_off/not_applicable; the scope reason did not hold (DEVLOG 2026-09-27, lane/idxaudit). lane/idxredstone 2026-09-27: exact. The plate's floor-loss drop went through place_block_drop, which only the placement probe's sink hears, so a live plate that lost its floor vanished without an item: blockcb.c now uses breaking_drop and randomtick.c break_draws drops the plates through the drops table (rs-wire-s1 failed at row 349 before). breakBlock's notification was missing (row 440). Stepping, releasing, the 20-tick re-check and the drops: rs-wire-s1; the weighted plates: plates-s1.
